To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HSP90 accelerates HIF-α protein accumulation under hypoxia.
the HIF-α PAS B domain binds to the chaperone HSP90, which is required for rapid hypoxia-induced stabilization of HIF-2 and HIF-1 α.
the HSP90 complex is involved in rapid HIF-α protein stabilization and that the PAS B domain mediates this interaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of HSP90 and ARNT with the PAS B domain and their role in the regulation of the hypoxic stabilization of the HIF-α subunits.
the interaction of HSP90 with the HIF-1/2/3α subunits.
the molecular mechanisms of HIF stabilization, which are important for the adaptation to hypoxia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HSP90 is involved in the regulation of hypoxia-dependent HIF-1 stabilization, but that HSP90 itself does not seem to be a limiting factor for the rapid hypoxic induction of HIF- 1.
HSP90 and ARNT interact with HIFs in a reciprocal and mutually exclusive manner.
HSP90 is required for HIF stabilization and that it may be a key factor in the very rapid stabilization of HIF- α proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HIF-1 complex contains at least three chaperones (HSP90, HSP70 and ARNT) that are involved in HIF-1 stabilization, folding and nuclear import.
the PAS B domain of HIF-2 and HIF-1 binds to HSP90 and that HSP90 is required for the rapid accumulation of HIF proteins.
HSP90 is involved in rapid HIF-α protein induction, which is mediated by the PAS B domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HSP90 accelerates HIF-1 stabilization under hypoxic conditions by facilitating the folding of HIF- α subunits.
HSP90 accelerates HIF-1 stabilization by binding to the PAS-B domain of HIF- 1 and that the interaction of ARNT with the PAS-B domain is required for HSP-90 release from HIF- 2.
HSP90 is a component of the HIF-1/ARNT heterotrimer and is required for rapid hypoxic HIF-1 stabilization.
